subject: Model fit & safety probes — post-demo runbook
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Model fit & safety probes — post-demo runbook

Hi Emily — great call today, thanks for walking through the primary use cases and the sample transcripts. This thread is a short runbook to align on next steps and the lightweight probes we'd recommend for the pilot.

Recap / win conditions we heard today
- Use case: clinician-facing summarization + triage suggestions for inbound referrals (medium-length clinical notes, some structured fields).
- Primary success metrics: information fidelity (ROUGE/EM-style checks on gold set), refusal/abstain rate on PHI-sensitive probes, average latency <= 300ms @ p95 for 512-token outputs, and cost target ~ $0.003 per generated token.

Recommended model candidates for the pilot (initial + fallback):
- Primary: Llama-3-70B (quantized q4f) — best quality for nuanced clinical reasoning and lower hallucination on our internal evals.
- Fallback: Llama-3-13B (q4) — much cheaper, good baseline for scale testing and as a graceful degradation path.

Safety / refusal evaluation plan (high level)
1) Prompt-set probes: 150 targeted prompts across PHI, self-harm, and treatment advice to verify refusal or safe completion. Link to prompt sets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/stratus-prompt-sets
2) Policy behavior metrics: measurable refusal rate, false-positive refusals, and risky completions flagged by automated policy classifiers.
3) Regression guardrails: keep a small canonical prompt/test harness to detect nightly regressions after any model change.

Attachments I'm sharing in the next email: benchmark summary (latency/cost), prompt set v1, and a draft SOW for pilot scope.

Proposed next steps
- Rishi/Monica: share benchmark numbers + prompt set (today) — ACTION: share files and short explainer.
- Emily: confirm pilot participants + target go/no-go date (we heard mid-June) — ACTION: confirm by EOD Tue.
- Schedule a 30-min alignment with your security lead to go through SOC2 + data handling (Monica to lead).

Three times that work for a follow-up demo with live probes: Wed 5/21 10:00am PT, Thu 5/22 2:00pm PT, Fri 5/23 11:00am PT. Please ping which one you prefer.

Thanks — Rishi

Emily — thanks, adding the numbers below and attaching the files. Quick answers inline.

On Tue, May 20, 2027 at 2:02 PM Rishi Malhotra wrote:
> Attachments: stratus_probe_promptset_v1.txt, benchmark-summary-20270520.pdf, pilot-sow-draft.docx

Benchmarks (local service-level runs, 512-token outputs)
- Llama-3-70B-q4f: p50 = 120ms, p95 = 260ms, avg cost = $0.0042 per generated token (note: this includes our batching efficiencies; hosted pricing may differ slightly). Refusal classification (policy guard): 97% correct refusal on our PHI probe suite, 2% false-positive refusals.
- Llama-3-13B-q4: p50 = 55ms, p95 = 140ms, avg cost = $0.0011 per generated token. Refusal classification: 92% correct refusal, 5% false-positive refusals.

Short notes on PHI probes: both models show high refusal for explicit patient-identifiable extraction (we attach a sample probe set). Edge cases: ambiguous prompts where the model infers context sometimes return a paraphrased safe summary rather than an abstain; we'll include explicit guardrail prompts that instruct refusal to reduce these.

Attachments (stubs):
- stratus_probe_promptset_v1.txt (contains the 150 targeted probes)
- benchmark-summary-20270520.pdf (detailed numbers and test harness)
- pilot-sow-draft.docx (pilot scope, deliverables, timeline)

Confirming Thu 5/22 2:00pm PT for the live probe session — we'll send calendar invite shortly. Monica will lead the security walkthrough and bring our SOC2 artifact. Ben will coordinate a lightweight success-metrics dashboard for the pilot.

Subject: Internal: quick notes on regression & guardrails before Wed

Rishi / Ben — short internal note before we go live tomorrow. We should be explicit about two items so the pilot doesn't become an open regression vector: 

1) Canonical regression set: keep a locked set of 30 synthetic + 20 real redacted examples that cover the top 8 failure modes (hallucination of medication, incorrect dates, incorrect patient attributes). Run nightly and gate changes.
2) Guardrail prompt templates: attach three quick templates we should inject server-side for the live probe session (examples below). These are enforced as a pre-prompt: 
- "If this request asks for patient-identifiable information, respond with 'I cannot assist with that request.'"
- "If the request asks for medical advice that requires diagnosis, respond with a safe, non-actionable summary and advise to consult a clinician."
- "When confidence < threshold, respond with 'I may be mistaken; please verify with the source document.'"

Also recommend tracking per-prompt drift: store per-prompt model output hash and a short diff to detect semantic drift after model updates. For candidate models: use 70B in canary for quality and 13B for load testing; do not expose 70B to external pilot users without canary gating.

I'll bring SOC2 and data retention notes to the security call.

—Monica
